layout_dets.text: A BSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pavement cracks are important information for evaluating the road condition and conducting the neces-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sary road maintenance. In this paper, we develop CrackTree, a fully-automatic method to detect cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from pavement images. In practice, crack detection is a very challenging problem because of (1) low con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trast between cracks and the surrounding pavement, (2) intensity inhomogeneity along the cracks, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3) possible shadows with similar intensity to the cracks. To address these problems, the proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method consists of three steps. First, we develop a geodesic shadow-removal algorithm to remove the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement shadows while preserving the cracks. Second, we build a crack probability map using tensor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: voting, which enhances the connection of the crack fragments with good proximity and curve continuity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, we sample a set of crack seeds from the crack probability map, represent these seeds by a graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model, derive minimum spanning trees from this graph, and conduct recursive tree-edge pruning to iden-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tify desirable cracks. We evaluate the proposed method on a collection of 206 real pavement images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a better performance than several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: existing methods.

layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cracks are common pavement distress that may potentially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threaten the road and highway safety. Fixing a crack before its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deterioration can greatly reduce the cost of pavement mainte-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nance. Since image-based technology provides a safe, efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and economical way for pavement crack detection, various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image-processing approaches have been proposed for pavement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection in the past two decades. Based on assumption that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the intensity along the cracks are usually lower than that of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background, i.e., the surrounding pavement, intensity thresholding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods (Kirschke and Velinsky, 1992; Oh et al., 1997; Li and Liu,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2008; Oliveira and Correia, 2009; Tsai et al., 2010) have been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: widely used for detecting cracks. However, these thresholding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods can only produce disjoint crack fragments because the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity along a crack may not be consistently lower than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background. Additionally, pavement shadows often incur an un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: even illuminance in the pavement images, which may further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decrease the performance of the thresholding methods. Edge-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection based methods have also been used for crack detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Yan et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2008; Ayenu-Prah and Attoh-Okine,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2008). However, the possible low contrast between the cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the background may misidentify many speckle noises in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background as crack fragments. Recently, wavelet-transform based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods (Zhou et al., 2006; Subirats et al., 2006) have been used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for crack detection. However, they may not handle well the cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with high curvature or bad continuity due to the anisotropic char-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acteristics of wavelets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Automatic detection of cracks from pavement images is a very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging problem. As shown in the original image in Fig. 1, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: many particle textures, the intensity of pavement is usually inho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mogeneous. While in general cracks bear intensities that are lower

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than the surrounding pavement, the contrast of cracks may be seri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ously weakened by possible cast shadows on the pavement and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possible crack degradations. As a result, local image-processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods, such as the intensity thresholding, edge detection, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sub-window based feature extraction methods (Cheng et al.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2001; Nguyen et al., 2009; Oliveira and Correia, 2008a,b) may have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difficulty in detecting the full crack curves: they usually detect a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set of disjoint crack fragments with many false positives.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we develop a new global method, called “Crack-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tree", for automatic crack detection. As shown by the flow chart

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 1, we first propose a new geodesic shadow-removal algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithm to remove the pavement shadows. Compared to many clas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sical shadow-removal algorithms (Finlayson et al., 2006, 2009;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Arbel and Hel-Or, 2007), the geodesic shadow-removal algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Over the past decades, the advance of the high-speed camera

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: technology and the large-storage hardware has made it easy to col-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lect pavement images of a long road in real time. As a result, auto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic crack detection through pavement image processing has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attracted more and more attention from both the academia and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the industry.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For its simplicity and efficiency, intensity-thresholding methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been widely used for crack detection. For example, the histo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gram-based method (Kirschke and Velinsky, 1992) and the iterated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clipping method (Oh et al., 1997) have been successfully used for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing images taken from the same pavement environment.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, they can not handle well the images from frequently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changed pavement environments. Li and Liu (2008) proposed a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neighboring difference histogram method (NDHM), which outper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms the classical thresholding methods, such as Otsu (1979) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kapur et al. (1985), on crack detection. However, by using a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threshold for the entire image, NDHM may fail when the images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contain uneven illuminance such as shadows. Tsai et al. (2010) re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cently suggested the use of a dynamic optimization based method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for segmenting low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) pavement images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This method, however, suffers from a high computation cost. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Oliveira and Correia, 2009), entropy is embedded into a two-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding framework for pavement crack detection.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Edge detection is another widely used technique for pavement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack detection. In (Ayenu-Prah and Attoh-Okine, 2008), the Sobel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge detector is applied to detect cracks after image smoothing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and speckle-noise removal using a bidimensional empirical mode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition algorithm. In (Yan et al., 2007), morphological fil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ters are introduced to detect crack edges with assistance of a mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ified median filter to remove noise. The major problem of using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge-detection based methods is their incapability of detecting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complete crack curves, and in most cases, they can only detect a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set of disjoint crack fragments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Wavelet transforms have also been exploited in pavement crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection. In (Zhou et al., 2006), road distresses, including cracks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are separated from noise and background using several statistical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: criteria based on wavelet coefficients. In (Subirats et al., 2006), a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2D continuous wavelet transform is applied to create multiscale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complex coefficient maps, on which the modulus and phase maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are constructed and a maxima location map is obtained for crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection. However, due to the anisotropic characteristic of wave-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lets, wavelet-based approaches may not handle well the cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with high curvature or low continuity.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Texture-analysis techniques have drawn extensive attention in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement crack detection since pavement images are highly tex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tured. Song et al. (1995) and Petrou et al. (1996) inspect cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a textured background using a Wigner model which can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve the best co-joint resolution in both spatial and frequency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domains. Hu and Zhao (2010) detect the pavement cracks through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: texture classification, which uses a local binary pattern operator

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Ojala et al., 2002) to distinguish the cracks and the background.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Many machine-learning techniques have been used in detecting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement cracks (Chou et al., 1995; Cheng et al., 2001; Nguyen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al., 2009; Oliveira and Correia, 2008a,b). In these methods, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement image is divided into a number of sub-images, each of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is represented by a vector of features extracted from this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sub-image. These sub-images are then used for the training and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classification for crack detection. In (Chou et al., 1995), a set of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moment invariants are computed as features, which are used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinguish different types of road distresses using a back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propagation (BP) neural network. The BP model is also used in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Nguyen et al., 2009), where an anisotropy measure is adopted as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the feature. In (Cheng et al., 2001), statistical values, such as mean

layout_dets.text: In addition, based on the assumption that crack pixels have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ceptual rules, such as proximity, continuity, and length.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Geodesic shadow removal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pavement images often suffer from cast shadows of trees, light

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poles, etc., along the road. In this section, we propose an algorithm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to remove such shadows for more accurate crack detection. Most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement images are gray without much color information. There-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fore, in this paper, we focus our algorithm development on mono-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromatic pavement images. In the following, we first present a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: texture-balanced illuminance compensation model to achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: even illumination in shadowed pavement images and then intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duce the proposed geodesic shadow-removal algorithm.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. MST construction and edge pruning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By using tensor voting, we expect that most pixels along the de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sired crack curves can receive more votes and stand out as local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maxima in the crack probability map. In this section, we develop

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a tree representation and pruning algorithm to further remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the image noise and other false positives.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.1. Crack seed sampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Crack seed sampling aims to reliably identify a set of crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seeds, which will be later connected into crack curves. On the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack probability map constructed in Section 4.2, we identify

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the local maxima as crack seeds. As illustrated in Fig. 4(f), if a pix-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: el A shows a locally maximal crack probability in any of the four

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directions defined in Fig. 4(g), we take A as a crack seed. Along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each direction, we search a range of ±rs pixels for determining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the local maxima, as illustrated in Fig. 4(f). In this paper, we pick

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5.2. MST construction and edge pruning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we develop an algorithm to connect crack seeds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to longer crack curves. Given that the cracks in a pavement image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack seeds that are far from each other. In connecting crack seeds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on the crack seeds, we construct an (undirected) graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to model the possible connections among these crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seeds. Specifically, for each crack seed, we construct a vertex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and for each pair of vertices v and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we check the Euclidean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distance between their corresponding crack seeds: if this distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is less than a pre-given threshold

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we construct an edge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to connect them and set its edge weight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be the Euclid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ean distance between these two crack seeds. Note that, G may not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be a connected graph and it may consist of several connected sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: graphs, as illustrated in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To identify the desired edge connections among crack seeds, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: find the minimum spanning tree (MST) from the constructed graph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: G. If G is not connected, we find the MST independently for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connected subgraph and put them together into a forest of trees.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MST is a spanning tree with the minimum total edge weight and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore, the edges that remain in an MST connect the crack seeds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the best proximity. Two examples of the MST construction are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig. 5(c) and (d).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In practice, we find that the derived MSTs may still include

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: undesirable edge connections. To address this problem, we further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conduct an edge pruning algorithm to remove the edges that show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very poor proximity and continuity. In this algorithm, crack curves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are recursively identified by searching for the longest path (the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: path with the largest total edge weights) among each possible pair

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of leaves in an MST. This algorithm is summarized in Algorithm 2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and an example is shown in Fig. 5(e)-(h).

layout_dets.text: 6. Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For performance evaluation, we collect a set of 206 pavement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images with various kinds of cracks. All these images have a size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 800 × 600, and many of them suffer from the problems of shad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ows, occlusions, low contrast, noise, etc. We manually annotate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground-truth crack curves on these images for objective perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance evaluation. We implement the proposed method in C++

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and test it on a Windows PC equipped with 2.4 GHz CPU and 2 M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RAM.

layout_dets.text: 7. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we developed CrackTree, a fully-automatic meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: od for detecting the crack curves from a pavement image. We first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introduced a new a geodesic shadow-removal algorithm to remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavement shadow and enhance the contrast of cracks. We then ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plied the tensor voting technique to construct a crack probability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: map by incorporating the perceptual cues of proximity and conti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nuity. We finally constructed minimum spanning trees (MSTs) to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: describe the possible connections of sampled crack seeds and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pruned undesired edges in this tree to achieve the final crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curves. We collected 206 pavement images with different kinds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of cracks to test the proposed method. Both the qualitative and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantitative comparison results show that the proposed CrackTree

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method outperforms several existing crack detection and edge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection algorithms.
